investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T23:17–23:24Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected by any check, confirming the agent pod never reached a schedulable state and the remote VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod was rejected by the scheduler on all 6 nodes: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for 133–144 seconds across all three checks, exceeding the eval timeout, so no VM was ever assigned and no evidence was written. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected by any check, and no preemption path was available, causing each probe to time out waiting for a schedulable node.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the remote agent pod: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as fully consumed (Insufficient), and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. This prevented createAgent() from ever returning a running pod, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes at eval run time — no capacity was available for a new remote agent pod, and preemption found no evictable victims.

[Likely contributing] The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the remote agent pod's node affinity or selector, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to only 2 nodes, making the feature sensitive to any concurrent VM usage.
[Possible] A concurrent workload or a prior eval run's pod was not cleaned up and is holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving zero capacity for the probe.

[Possible] The node affinity or selector on the remote agent pod template is overly restrictive, excluding 4 of 6 nodes from ever being eligible, which reduces the effective VM pool size and increases the likelihood of exhaustion.
[Lower confidence] A cluster scaling event or node maintenance reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent eval probes.
